15 A crate of mass 50 kg is pushed a distance of 6.0 m along a horizontal surface against a constant
resistive force of 70 N. The crate moves at a constant speed. It is then lifted, at a constant speed,
through a vertical distance of 1.2 m onto the back of a lorry.
What is the total work done in this process?
A
420 J
B
480 J
C
590 J
D
1000 J

hints: Notice the process has two parts: a $6.0 \text{ m}$ horizontal push against a $70 \text{ N}$ resistive force, then a $1.2 \text{ m}$ vertical lift of a $50 \text{ kg}$ mass.
Recall that constant speed means no gain in kinetic energy, so work is done against resistance in stage 1 with $W = Fd$ and against weight in stage 2 with $W = mgh$.
Calculate the $70 \text{ N}$ by $6.0 \text{ m}$ work and the $mg$ by $1.2 \text{ m}$ work separately, then add them for the total work.
walkthrough: Identify the two stages: horizontal displacement $d = 6.0 \text{ m}$ against $F = 70 \text{ N}$, and vertical height $h = 1.2 \text{ m}$ for mass $m = 50 \text{ kg}$.
For constant speed, the pushing force equals the resistive force, so horizontal work is $W_h = Fd$.
For the lift at constant speed, the lifting force equals weight $mg$, so vertical work is $W_v = mgh$.
Substitute with $g = 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$: $W_v = 50 \times 9.81 \times 1.2 = 588.6 \text{ J}$, about $590 \text{ J}$.
Add both contributions: $W_{total} = 420 + 588.6 = 1008.6 \text{ J}$, about $1000 \text{ J}$ to the given precision. This is option D.

A.explanation: This is only the horizontal work $W = 70 \times 6.0 = 420 \text{ J}$ and omits the work to lift the crate.

B.explanation: This matches neither stage and is far below the sum of the $420 \text{ J}$ horizontal work plus about $590 \text{ J}$ of lifting work.

C.explanation: This is only the lifting work $W = mgh$ of about $590 \text{ J}$ and omits the $420 \text{ J}$ done pushing horizontally.

D.explanation: This is the sum of horizontal work $420 \text{ J}$ and lifting work about $590 \text{ J}$, giving about $1000 \text{ J}$.
